title: guardrail-config.v1
description: Global execution guardrails: when a channel may be contacted and how often (plan §7 DEC-4/DEC-16). Published and versioned exactly like a rule set — immutable once PUBLISHED, `GuardrailConfigPublished` on activation — because "who changed the SMS window?" is an audit question. These guardrails are re-evaluated by treatment-service immediately BEFORE dispatch, not only at decision time: a decision taken at 20:59 that reaches the dispatcher at 21:01 is window-blocked and rescheduled, and a customer who has just been contacted by another process is capped. Violations produce SUPPRESSED with `CONTACT_WINDOW_BLOCKED` / `FREQUENCY_CAP_EXCEEDED`, never a dispatch, and the guardrail check fails closed: if the caps cannot be evaluated the treatment is suppressed (`POLICY_RECHECK_UNAVAILABLE`), never sent on the assumption that it was probably fine.

configId.description: Stable identifier of the guardrail configuration family, e.g. `GLOBAL_GUARDRAILS`.

version.description: Major version, starting at 1 and incremented on every publish. Decisions and treatments record the version they were checked against.

contactWindows.description: Permitted local contact window per channel — at most one entry per channel (DEC-4 rejects duplicates; the schema cannot compare siblings). A channel with NO entry is unrestricted by time, so an omission is permissive: DEC-4 requires an explicit entry for every channel a published strategy can dispatch on, which turns a forgotten channel into a publish-time 400 instead of an out-of-hours SMS.

frequencyCaps.description: Contact frequency caps. Every applicable cap is enforced and the most restrictive wins — an `ALL`-channel cap and a channel-specific cap coexist deliberately (e.g. at most 6 contacts in 30 days overall, at most 2 SMS in 7 days).

startLocal.description: Inclusive start of the window as a local wall-clock time `HH:MM` in `timezone`. Wall-clock rather than UTC because the rule being encoded is a regulatory/courtesy one about the customer's day, and it must not drift by an hour when daylight saving changes.

endLocal.description: Exclusive end of the window, `HH:MM` local. `endLocal` > `startLocal` is required (validated by DEC-4): windows do not wrap past midnight, so a night-time window is expressed as two entries rather than one that silently inverts.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name the local times are interpreted in, e.g. `Europe/Dublin`. Defaults to `UTC`, which is also what the platform stores and logs everywhere else (CLAUDE.md §3) — this field is the one place a local offset legitimately enters a contract, and it is a zone name rather than an offset so that DST is resolved from tzdata rather than assumed.

channel.description: Channel the cap counts, or `ALL` for a cross-channel cap counting every channel together.

windowDays.description: Rolling window in whole days, counted back from the dispatch instant (not a calendar week): a 7-day cap on Monday morning counts the previous Monday morning onwards.

maxContacts.description: Maximum contact attempts permitted in the window. 0 means the channel is effectively disabled by guardrail — legal, and clearer than deleting the entry, because a deleted entry means "unrestricted".
